column1: # English for 속담 (proverbs) and 성어 (four-character idioms) that krdict has no entry for (the 18 proverbs of
# study list sokdam100 and the 246 성어 kept by qa/frequency/seongeo_review.tsv that only stdict/opendict have).
# Merged into the core pack as source 'hanppuri' entries (kind proverb for 속담, word for 성어) -- but ONLY rows whose
# review column starts with "approved"; everything else stays here as a draft.  The Korean source line (stdict/opendict)
# Tab-separated; the first column says which kind of row it is. Rows of one item are grouped:
# the P row, then its E rows (examples, in display order).
#   P  kind  headword  hanja  src  en_gloss  en_def  ko_def  review
# headword    as the study list shows it (no hanja in brackets); an E row repeats it.
# hanja       the four characters of a 성어 (empty for 속담).
# src         stdict:<ext_id> | opendict:<ext_id>: the pack entry the Korean definition is copied from (and the
#             entry the study list points at).
# en_gloss    short krdict-style English meaning; an established English idiom only where it truly matches. AI-written.
# en_def      one-sentence English definition; for a 성어 it ends with the literal reading of the hanja,
# ko_def      Korean definition, copied VERBATIM from the entry's first sense in the pack named by src
#             (qa: tests/idiom_extra.rs checks it against the packs when they are built locally, and the build
# review      draft | approved[:who/date]. Written as draft; only an independent review (content-review skill,
#             qa/idiom_english_review.md) may change it. Only approved rows ship.
# ko_source   stdict | opendict (copied verbatim from that dictionary entry) | ai (written for this file; only
#             where the dictionary entry has fewer than two full example sentences).
# Every AI-written field is listed in qa/idiom_english_review.md for an independent check;
# nothing here counts as reviewed until that file says so.
